checks.remediation: Reinstall on Ubuntu 25.10 or 26.04 LTS. Older releases lack the TDX kernel support this stack needs.
checks.title: Ubuntu release is supported

checks.remediation: BIOS: enable Intel TDX (and TME / TME-MT) in the CPU security menu. The kernel must be Canonical intel or mainline 6.16 or newer.
checks.title: Intel TDX is enabled

checks.remediation: BIOS: enable VT-d / Intel Virtualization Technology for Directed I/O. Without it no device can be passed through to a TD guest.
checks.title: VT-d / IOMMU is enabled

checks.remediation: BIOS: enable Intel SGX and set PRMRR size to 64M or more. An SGX Factory Reset may be required.
checks.title: SGX device nodes are present

checks.expected: /boot/grub/grub.cfg exists and update-grub is on PATH
checks.remediation: This host does not boot via GRUB (systemd-boot or a vendor bootloader). Apply the docs/host-setup.md section 2 kernel parameters by hand and re-run with --skip-tags kernel.
checks.title: This host boots via GRUB

checks.remediation: Searched PCI ids: 10de:2335, 10de:2336, 10de:2330, 10de:233a. If lspci is missing, install pciutils. If your GPU is CC-capable but not in that list it is not yet supported.
checks.title: A confidential-compute capable GPU is present

checks.expected: more than 0 rows in the pck_cert table
checks.remediation: Set lium_intel_api_key to run a local PCCS and in-band registration; otherwise DCAP collateral comes from https://localhost:8081/sgx/certification/v4/. With 0 certificates the sealing-key enclave crash-loops with "AESM service returned error 44". Read the pck_cert row count, never /var/log/mpa_registration.log, which reports success on broken hosts too.
checks.title: This platform has PCK certificates

checks.remediation: systemctl status pccs. A PCCS that dies with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: config needs `npm install` in /opt/intel/sgx-dcap-pccs — the interactive postinst wizard normally does that and it fails under apt.
checks.title: The PCCS service is running

checks.remediation: Uncomment `port = 4050` in /etc/qgs.conf and restart qgsd. It ships commented out, so qgsd serves a unix socket instead, reports active, and never answers the guest — the CVM then reboots at around 160 seconds with "vsock failure: Connection reset by peer (os error 104)".
checks.title: qgsd serves TD quotes over vsock

checks.remediation: Set "use_secure_cert": false in /etc/sgx_default_qcnl.conf AND in key-provider/sgx_default_qcnl.conf. Intel ships the system one as true, which rejects a local self-signed PCCS certificate: "[QCNL] CURL error: (60)", "[QPL] ... 0xb033", then the guest reboots.
checks.title: The QPL accepts the PCCS certificate

checks.expected: the file parses once whole-line // comments are stripped
checks.remediation: Re-run the sgx role: it writes this file whole from a template with a json.load validate, so it cannot install an unparseable one. The pristine platform copy is kept at /etc/sgx_default_qcnl.conf.pre-lium-cvm. This is checked separately from sgx.qpl_secure_cert_false because that check GREPS for a key, and a grep is satisfied by a line appended after the closing brace — which is exactly how a corrupted file passed while the QPL could not read a word of it. Symptom: every CVM reboots at ~160s, "cpus are not resettable, terminating", and docker logs dstack-key-provider shows "DCAP error".
checks.title: The QPL configuration is readable JSON

checks.expected: PRODUCTION mode, RestartCount 0, no enclave errors
checks.observed: running=true, restarts=0, production lines=1, enclave errors=0
checks.remediation: This is the end-to-end proof that the whole SGX chain works. "error 44" or a failed load_enclave means the platform has no PCK certificates — fix sgx.registration_pck_certs first.
checks.title: The sealing-key provider runs in production mode

checks.remediation: Egress filtering is common in provider datacenters, and an unreachable Intel API turns in-band registration into an opaque hang. Allow outbound TCP to api.trustedservices.intel.com:443, or use a remote PCCS via lium_pccs_url.
checks.title: Intel's provisioning API is reachable

checks.expected: every GPU reports CC mode on
checks.remediation: CC mode is OFF by default on a fresh host. It is a hardware prerequisite for GPU passthrough into a TD guest — ENABLE_GPU_ATTESTATION=false does NOT make it optional. Re-run the gpu role.
checks.title: Every GPU has confidential-compute mode on

checks.expected: every GPU and NVSwitch bound to vfio-pci
checks.remediation: Re-run the gpu role. Binding the GPUs but not the NVSwitches produces a guest that boots and then cannot see NVLink.
checks.title: Every GPU and NVSwitch is bound to vfio-pci

checks.remediation: None. Recorded so a device that disappears between runs is visible — a hot-removed GPU is what makes vfio-pci.ids= try to narrow.

checks.remediation: The shipped default is 65535, which kills a TD guest mid-boot with "VFIO_MAP_DMA failed: No space left on device" because TDX shared/private page conversions exhaust it.
checks.title: The vfio DMA entry limit is raised

checks.remediation: The runtime write applies immediately but does not survive a reboot. Re-run the kernel role.
checks.title: The DMA entry limit survives a reboot

checks.observed: 0 token(s) missing from the running kernel
checks.remediation: Re-run bootstrap.sh and allow the reboot. If it has already rebooted twice without effect, check whether /boot is full and whether update-grub actually rewrote grub.cfg.
checks.title: The running kernel has every required parameter

checks.expected: every required token wins in GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX plus GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT
checks.observed: 0 token(s) not resolving in the merged GRUB configuration
checks.remediation: Re-run the kernel role. The drop-in appends to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT and never assigns GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX, so a provider value is never clobbered.
checks.title: The kernel parameters are persisted in GRUB

checks.remediation: These keys appear more than once with different values. Ours win, because 10_linux emits GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX before GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT and the kernel takes the last occurrence — but relying on that ordering forever is fragile. Remove the stale copies from /etc/default/grub.
checks.title: No stale duplicate kernel parameters

checks.remediation: Attestation fails on RTMR0 if the host runs distro QEMU instead of the dstack build. Re-run the qemu role.
checks.title: The dstack QEMU build is installed

checks.remediation: Read from /etc/dstack/client.conf directly. Do not use `lium-cvm.sh check` for this: it looks on PATH while the launcher uses client.conf, so it reports a false MISSING on a correctly configured host.
checks.title: dstack points at the right QEMU

checks.remediation: QEMU is a measured input. A binary that changed underneath a running CVM means RTMR0 no longer matches and any existing hda.img is undecryptable. Investigate before restarting anything.
checks.title: The QEMU binary is unchanged since it was installed

checks.remediation: The ref was not moved because this host still holds CVM state, and moving it rewrites the measured surface. Upgrading a host that has a CVM is a deliberate procedure: see docs/host-setup.md section 6.

checks.remediation: Per-executor .env stays manual: see docs/host-setup.md section 5. Presence only is reported here, never a comparison against a whitelist — a checkout can be BEHIND the deployed validator, and on one occasion the whitelisted digest was the broken one. Do not downgrade to match a local list.
checks.title: The executor runner digest is set

checks.remediation: None. Recorded so the report shows what was listening at the time of the run.
checks.title: Local listening sockets

checks.expected: an off-site read test confirms the executor ports are reachable
checks.remediation: ss proves a port is LISTENING, never that it is REACHABLE. Two hosts silently blackholed 8001/2200/19001 while permitting 22 and 30000-32767, and everything looked perfect from the host itself. Probe from an independent network with a READ test (exec 3<>/dev/tcp/HOST/PORT && head -c 2 <&3), and calibrate that vantage against a dead port on a well-known third party first — many networks forge SYN-ACKs for every destination, which makes a plain connect test worthless. Fixing datacenter ACLs is out of scope for this playbook.
checks.title: Port reachability must be checked from outside
